# AP-INC-002 Operational Incident Response and Review

## 1. Purpose and Scope  
This policy establishes the procedures for reporting, coordinating, and reviewing operational incidents at AeroPolicy Airport. It ensures a timely and consistent response to incidents that may affect safety, security, or operational efficiency. The policy applies to all incidents within the airport’s airside and landside operations, including but not limited to baggage handling, restricted-item discovery, ramp safety, and equipment malfunctions. All staff are required to report incidents in accordance with this policy to maintain a safe and secure environment for passengers, employees, and aircraft operations.

## 2. Incident Categories  
Operational incidents are categorized into four types: baggage incidents, restricted-item incidents, ramp safety incidents, and equipment incidents. Baggage incidents include any issues related to the handling, loading, or unloading of luggage. Restricted-item incidents involve the discovery of prohibited items in aircraft or restricted areas. Ramp safety incidents encompass any hazards or accidents on the ramp area. Equipment incidents refer to malfunctions or failures of operational equipment. Each category has specific procedures for reporting and escalation, as outlined in related policies.

## 3. Reporting and First Response  
Any staff member who witnesses or becomes aware of an operational incident must immediately report it to their supervisor or the Airside Duty Manager. The Reporting Staff Member is responsible for providing a clear and accurate description of the incident, including location, time, and any immediate actions taken. In the case of a baggage incident, the Reporting Staff Member must follow the procedures outlined in AP-BAG-001 section 4. For restricted-item incidents, the procedures in AP-SEC-003 must be followed. The Airside Duty Manager is responsible for initiating the first response and ensuring that the incident is properly documented.

## 4. Incident Coordinator Duties  
The Incident Coordinator is responsible for managing the response to operational incidents and ensuring that all necessary actions are taken to mitigate risks and prevent recurrence. The Incident Coordinator must open an incident record for every reported incident before the end of the shift in which it was reported. This record includes details of the incident, initial response actions, and any relevant documentation. The Incident Coordinator also coordinates with relevant departments and ensures that all required follow-up actions are initiated. The Incident Coordinator is accountable for the timely and accurate communication of incident details to all stakeholders.

## 5. Post-Incident Review  
Following the resolution of an incident, a review meeting is conducted to analyze the incident and identify root causes. The review meeting is led by the Incident Coordinator and includes representatives from relevant departments. During the meeting, the cause of the incident is thoroughly examined, and corrective actions are identified to prevent similar incidents in the future. All participants are required to provide input and documentation to support the review process. The meeting results in a formal report that is reviewed by senior management and used to update procedures and training programs. The review process ensures continuous improvement in operational safety and efficiency.

## 6. Records  
All incident records must be maintained in a secure and accessible location for the duration required by regulatory authorities and internal policy. Records include incident reports, corrective action plans, and meeting minutes from post-incident reviews. Each record is assigned a unique identifier and is stored in a centralized database. Access to records is restricted to authorized personnel only. Records are reviewed periodically to ensure their accuracy and completeness. All records are retained for a minimum of five years, unless otherwise specified by applicable regulations. The records serve as a reference for training, audits, and continuous improvement initiatives.
